sections.html:
A buyer willing to take your house untouched cuts out much of the repair list, the open houses and the back-and-forth that usually come before a closing. Listing with an agent or selling privately remains possible too. All three paths finish with a condition report from you, a transfer return and a deed that gets recorded.

Mequon sits in Ozaukee County and counts 25,120 residents. Owners live in about 86.0% of the homes, and the median owner-occupied home was worth $501,600 for 2020 to 2024. Prices like that make every credit and every markdown a big number, so many sellers compare an as-is offer against the dollars and months a full fix-up would take.

sections.h2: City sewer and water, or well and septic?
sections.html:
What reaches your lot depends on where it sits. Some Mequon parcels receive city water and sewer, others only one of the two, and a few neither. City sewer covers the sanitary sewer service areas, and the septic and mound systems fall outside them. The Mequon Water Utility supplies Mequon, Thiensville and Bayside, but a good number of homes continue to rely on a private well or a water trust.

You need the answer early because the state condition report includes a section on wells, septic systems and storage tanks. Phone the Sewer and Water Utilities office and have them confirm how your address is served.

  • Water comes from the Mequon Water Utility, a private well or a water trust.
  • Sewer comes from the city system inside a sanitary sewer service area, or from a septic or mound system.
  • Set aside any septic, well or tank paperwork you already own, since a buyer may ask to see it.

The utility reports no lead water mains and no lead service lines, and plastic laterals have been required since service began in 1998. Inside a house, lead can still show up in solder on copper plumbing from before 1986 and in brass faucets and fittings from before 2014. If yours is an older house, an inspector may point at those fixtures.

Nearly all of Mequon belongs to the Mequon-Thiensville School District. Roughly six square miles in the far northwest are part of the Cedarburg School District instead, which matters if your street is near that boundary. Parents shopping for a house tend to open with this question, so state the district in your listing and spare them the call.

Transit is limited. One weekday commuter route to Milwaukee, the Ozaukee County Express (Route 143), serves the city, with a shared-ride taxi for trips beyond it. Many areas have no sidewalks, which a buyer on foot or with a stroller will notice.

sections.h2: City offices you will deal with
sections.html:
Zoning, planning and permit forms all run through Community Development. To book an inspection, dial (262) 236-2930. A finished permit application can be handed in during office hours, sent by mail or email, or left in the drop box east of the southern main door at City Hall.

The Assessor's Office works from the Wisconsin Property Assessment Manual and Chapter 70 of the state statutes, and Department of Revenue certification is held by every staff member. Anyone wanting detailed assessment or property tax answers is directed to City Hall. Request the current assessment before you pick a list price. Property tax and utility bills can be paid through links on the city website.

sections.h2: What Wisconsin asks of a Mequon seller
sections.html:
Selling triggers a real estate transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value, owed by the seller under Wis. Stat. 77.22. For a property with one to four dwelling units, the buyer must also receive your condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted.

  • Skip that deadline and the buyer has 2 business days after the 10-day period to rescind and recover deposits.
  • Learn something new before accepting an offer, and Wis. Stat. 709.035 asks for an amended report within 10 days of acceptance.
  • The Department of Revenue exempts some transfers from the fee, among them transfers by will or descent and those between parent and child for nominal or no consideration.
  • An understated value on the return risks a penalty of $25 or 25% of the additional fee, whichever is greater.

The return is filed electronically with the Department of Revenue. For questions, email its return team at RETR@wisconsin.gov.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Ozaukee County
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the Ozaukee County Register of Deeds, 121 W. Main Street, Room 120, Port Washington. Counter hours run 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. Call 262-284-8260, or mail documents to P.O. Box 994, Port Washington, WI 53074.

The register also offers a Property Fraud Alert sign-up and a Designation of Transfer on Death form. After recording, each transfer appears in the Land Information Office's property transfer report with its fee, parcel number, grantor and grantee. Anyone can divide the fee by 3 and multiply by 1,000 to get the sale price, so assume your price will be visible.

Your documents decide how smoothly a sale goes. Before you list, gather the following.

  • The answer on whether you have city water, city sewer, a well or a septic system.
  • Any septic, well or storage tank paperwork.
  • Permit records for past work. Community Development can help with an inspection question.
  • The current-year assessment from City Hall.
  • Your school district, confirmed against the address.

Sellers with a lakefront or large rural lot should add one more check, because lot sizes and available services vary widely across the city.

Make the utilities call first, because the well, septic or city service answer feeds directly into the condition report. Next, pull permit paperwork and get the assessment. Once an offer is accepted, the 10-day report period begins. During it, you or the title company file the transfer return, and then the deed goes to Port Washington for recording.

An as-is cash buyer spares you the repair requests that tend to follow an inspection. The report, the return and the recording stay on the list regardless. Get the closing date in writing, along with who pays for title work.

faqs.q: Does every Mequon house have city sewer and water?
faqs.a: No. Some properties have both services, some only water or only sewer, and some neither. Many still use a private well or a septic or mound system. Call the Sewer and Water Utilities office to confirm what serves your address.
The Mequon-Thiensville School District covers most of the city. About six square miles in the far northwest fall in the Cedarburg School District.

faqs.q: How do I schedule a building inspection in Mequon?
faqs.a: Phone Community Development at (262) 236-2930. Finished permit applications can be handed in, mailed or emailed, or left in the drop box east of City Hall's southern main door.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer fee on a Mequon house sale?
faqs.a: You do, as the seller, at 30 cents per $100 of value. The register collects it with the deed unless the transfer is exempt.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Mequon house?
faqs.a: At the Ozaukee County Register of Deeds, 121 W. Main Street, Room 120, Port Washington. It opens Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the phone is 262-284-8260.
